ov: The common eland, a huge spiral-horned antelope of the plains and open woodland of East and southern Africa. Both sexes have horns. It lives in loose herds of up to 500, feeds mainly at dawn and dusk, and has been farmed for its meat and rich milk.

why.et: Hunted and farmed for its meat; some southern African farmers have switched from cattle to eland because it suits the climate better.
why.dm: Kept and farmed in southern Africa and Russia, but it has not been bred into a distinct domestic form.

ht: Males 150–183 cm, females 125–153 cm at the shoulder
rg: East and southern Africa, from Ethiopia and South Sudan south to South Africa and west to Angola and Namibia.
df: Leaves of flowering plants, plus grasses, forbs, seeds, tubers and fruit. It gets most of its water from its food.
fx: Herds make a loud clicking as they walk, probably the two halves of each hoof snapping together.
Its milk has 11–17% butterfat and, properly prepared, keeps for up to eight months.
